Flat-figure Core Concept supplies rectangle P=2(l+w) and A=lw for #1; parallelogram A=bh and triangle A=bh/2 for #2; trapezoid A=(b1+b2)h/2 for #3; square A=s squared, radius d/2, circle A=pi r squared, and Combined Regions subtraction for #4.

Rectangle area, same-unit requirement, 1 m=100 cm, and nonoverlap addition prepare #5. Solids supplies rectangular prism V=lwh and SA=2(lw+lh+wh) for #6 and cylinder V=pi r squared h and SA=2 pi r squared+2 pi rh for #7.

Cone V=pi r squared h/3 and ell squared=r squared+h squared appear in Core Concept before #8. Sphere V=4 pi r cubed/3 and SA=4 pi r squared prepare #9. Rectangle base area and pyramid V=Bh/3 prepare #10.

Cube V=e cubed and SA=6e squared plus k=new/old, Vnew=k cubed Vold, and surface-area scaling k squared prepare #11. Area scaling k squared, positive-square-root reversal, and perimeter scaling k prepare #12.

Examples cover reverse perimeter, slanted-side rejection in two flat shapes, trapezoid, contained-region subtraction, mixed-unit composite addition, box, cylinder, cone, sphere, pyramid, forward solid scaling, and reverse area-to-perimeter scaling. They progress from basic measurements to combined and inverse tasks without near-duplicate solutions.

Every multistep computation is numbered and its key arithmetic displayed. Radius conversion, three box-face areas, cone volume, and inverse scale extraction are all explicit. The postscript after #9 adds a unit observation without hiding a solving step.
Scanned all example displays and Core Concept equations; long evaluations are split, including cone, sphere, pyramid, and box calculations. Each display is short enough for a phone.
Teaching paragraphs contain one to three sentences. Two compact formula lists group six flat shapes and six solids; remaining prose is in short paragraphs.

Shape gallery specifies labels and perpendicular markers. All twelve example placeholders specify the needed dimensions, geometry, or shaded region. #5 describes how the rectangles attach. Questions and solutions give enough information to solve without the figures.

Perimeter, area, volume, surface area, base, perpendicular height, radius, diameter, pi, symbols, slant height, and scale factor are locally explained. Inscribed is explained in its question by touching all sides.

findings.quote: Two similar rectangles have areas of $20\text{ cm}^2$ and $180\text{ cm}^2$.
findings.problem: Similar is needed to understand why an area ratio determines a length ratio. Its meaning is first given in the solution, after the question requires it. Core Concept describes uniform scaling but never identifies similar figures as figures with this relationship. No prerequisite or later-explanation signpost supplies that term before use.

checked: Measurements explain what is counted and which unit power applies. Cylinder volume uses stacked base areas; cylinder surface area uses an unrolled rectangle and two ends. Cone slant height explains the right triangle and Pythagorean relationship. Scaling explains powers through the number of length dimensions; combined regions explains addition versus subtraction.

Checked perpendicular heights, same length units, closed-cylinder ends, right-cone geometry, matching cone/cylinder and pyramid/prism comparisons, positive roots, containment/nonoverlap, and uniform positive scale factor conditions. All relevant restrictions are stated.
The flagged right-angle mark is a geometric symbol, not a score. No score is called marks and no questions are called cards.
